question: The presence of an electron-withdrawing group in the chain of the acyl group of penicillins increases its stability in an acidic medium because:

options.opa: Increases the basicity of bridge nitrogen.
options.opb: Decreases the nucleophilicity of amidic oxygen in the chain.

analysis: The presence of an electron-withdrawing group in the acyl side chain of penicillins stabilizes the molecule in acidic conditions by decreasing the nucleophilicity of the amidic oxygen. This reduces the likelihood of the penicillin undergoing acid-catalyzed hydrolysis, which is a common degradation pathway. By decreasing the nucleophilicity, the electron-withdrawing group makes the carbonyl carbon less susceptible to nucleophilic attack, thereby enhancing the stability of the penicillin in acidic environments.
